question.problem:
| **Age, in years ($x$)** | $6$ | $10$ | $12$ | $16$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Education, in years ($y$)** | $2$ | $4$ | $8$ | $10$ |

The table above shows the ages and corresponding years of formal education completed by each of Mark's cousins.
Compute the covariance of the data sets given that the means are $\overset{―}{x}=11$ and $\overset{―}{y}=6.$
question.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(6-11)(2-6)+(10-11)(4-6)+(12-11)(8-6)+(16-11)(10-6)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-5)(-4)+(-1)(-2)+(1)(2)+(5)(4)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[20+2+2+20] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 44 \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$
